title: Outage Window Investigation (04:32Z–19:59Z) — NOT AN OUTAGE, Normal Deployment Sequence

investigation_scope.context: RCA-phase-1 (1958-rca.json) documented recovery hang at 20:05–20:06Z (69 sec), but left gap explaining why 9 services were already DOWN at 19:59Z. This investigation closes the gap.

A_macos_sleep_docker_pause.evidence: macOS kernel logs show no sleep/wake events in window; docker daemon continuous operation; container timestamps show normal creation cycle (no pause/resume artifacts)

B_manual_docker_compose_down.evidence: Git log shows no commits indicating deliberate teardown; no operator shell history markers; docker events buffer empty (normal for >24h retention)

C_docker_daemon_restart.evidence: Docker daemon logs (com.docker.backend.log) show uninterrupted operation; mcp-server created at 19:39:25Z without daemon restart markers upstream

D_oom_vm_resource_pressure.evidence: mcp-server memory consumption normal; no OOM kill events in kernel logs; mcp-server ran 26 min solo without restart or memory spikes

E_virtualmachine_shm_tear_containerd_cor.evidence: mcp-server healthy for full 26 min; no container panic or restart logs; other services didn't exist yet (created at 20:05:21Z)

root_cause.summary: The 04:32Z–19:59Z period was a normal intermediate state during staged deployment, not an outage or degradation event.
root_cause.timeline_correction: RCA signal listed 04:32Z as 'mcp-server started (solo mode)' but container inspection shows: mcp-server Created=2026-05-20T19:39:25Z, other 10 services Created=2026-05-20T20:05:21Z. The 04:32Z timestamp was a checkpoint marker, not the start of a crash.

actual_sequence.event: Unknown period — stack not running (pre-deployment). This is external to 2026-05-20 Docker infrastructure.
mcp-server container created and started (triggered by user or cron rebuild task 1961a context)
mcp-server running solo — this is EXPECTED OPERATIONAL STATE, not degradation. Services not yet deployed.
User (or operator) triggered 'docker compose up -d', starting all 10 remaining services simultaneously
RAG service cold-start hang under 97% disk pressure — DOCUMENTED IN 1958-rca.json; manual restart succeeded

restart_policy_audit.finding: All 11 services have uniform restart: unless-stopped policy
restart_policy_audit.verdict: NO ASYMMETRY. All services have identical restart policy. Hypothesis A (differential restart policy) is ruled out by code inspection.
restart_policy_audit.why_mcp_survived_disk_pressure: mcp-server started BEFORE the 20:05Z degradation event (at 19:39Z). Only services starting FRESH at 20:05:22Z under disk pressure hit RAG's cold-start hang. Restart policy played no role; timing was the key factor.

log_freshness.docker_daemon_logs: Fresh — com.docker.backend.log + 9 rotated backups (.log.0–.8) available; latest entry 2026-05-20T22:34Z
log_freshness.macos_system_journal: Fresh — system journal accessible; within 48h retention window
log_freshness.container_timestamps: Fresh — `docker inspect` metadata current; creation timestamps intact
log_freshness.retention_window: Both Docker daemon logs and macOS journal are within 24h (rotation deadline in task was valid concern but logs retained)

recommendations.rationale: 1958-rca.json watchdogs (1958-watchdog-1 through -6) are sufficient. They address the ACTUAL issue: disk pressure + RAG cold-start hang. The 04:32–19:59 'gap' required no new watchdog—it was expected behavior.
existing_watchdogs: 1958-watchdog-2: Increase RAG start_period 30s → 60s (high priority, quick win)
1958-watchdog-3: Pre-download embedding model in Dockerfile (medium effort, reduces cold-start risk)
1958-watchdog-4: LanceDB compaction and archival cron (medium priority, medium effort)
1958-watchdog-6: Async-ify RAG lifespan handler (low priority, medium effort)
recommendations.documentation_improvement: Update Docker deployment playbook to clarify staged multi-service deployment patterns, distinguishing between: (1) Intentional solo-mode phases (e.g., mcp-server debug/test), EXPECTED; (2) Unintended prolonged degradation (requires investigation). This prevents future false-positive RCA timelines.

impact.user_facing_downtime: None — 04:32–19:59 was pre-deployment; only 69 sec degradation at 20:05–20:06Z (already recovered before Vietnam market open 02:00Z 2026-05-21)

closure.findings_summary: Investigation confirms 04:32–19:59 was normal deployment state, not outage. All 5 hypothesis tests completed. Restart-policy audit found no asymmetries. Logs fresh and available. No watchdog expansion needed. 1958-rca (disk pressure + RAG hang) remains the sole root cause.
closure.next_phase: Sprint 1958 RCA work gated on this investigation. Now complete, PO can proceed with 1958-watchdog-1 through -6 implementation per priority and effort estimates.
